purpose: Provenance for the full-data popularity fill order published beside the pinned SASRec encoder (W21). The bytes themselves carry none of this on purpose - anything inside them would make the artifact unreproducible from its documented inputs - so this is where it lives until a served bundle's manifest Lineage carries it.

encoder.note: sasrec-manifest.json is deliberately NOT rewritten: a published bundle pins its bytes under the vocabulary and config roles, so the fill order is attached by fixed filename here and pinned by the serving manifest.

inputs.training_frame: temporal_split(ratings).train with the ADR 0011 cohort history attached, i.e. the frame SASRecModel.fit fitted its PopularityModel on

ordering.rule: interaction count descending, then movieId ascending
ordering.why_stated: PopularityModel.fit sorts with pandas' default quicksort, which is not stable, so its order among equal-count movies is an implementation detail that can move between versions. Fine for a ranking, not fine for bytes a manifest pins by SHA-256.

reproduction.machine: Apple silicon macOS, no other job on the box at the time

verification.cold_routed_user_now_answered: recommend(unknown_user, 5) -> [356, 296, 318, 593, 480]; before this change a bundle loaded from disk returned nothing
